$comment: Bundle boundaries (design/12 'Bundle boundaries' + 'the first download is code only',
design/04 WeChat package limits).
This file is the ONE place a shipped asset's package membership is decided, and it is
read by three consumers on purpose: the TypeScript runtime (render/assetManifest.ts,
which rewrites a path into its packed location), plain Node in the build
(build/wechatAssetSync.mjs), and the byte gate (build/checkWeChatPackage.mjs). A JSON
file is the only shape all three can read without a build step, which is what keeps
them from drifting apart.
WeChat's real limits (official 分包 docs, re-checked 2026-08-25): main package <= 4 MB,
a standard subpackage has NO individual cap, an INDEPENDENT subpackage <= 4 MB, and the
whole game (main + every subpackage) <= 30 MB.
THE MAIN PACKAGE IS CODE AND NOTHING ELSE (2026-09-01). Until then every pack was fetched
at boot by `ensureAllPacks()`, which satisfied the 4 MB rule (it is a rule about the FIRST
download) and bought nothing else: art still occupied 2.49 MB of the 4.00 MB, so `js/game.js`
had 2,729 bytes of headroom and the next code change of any size failed the gate. That is what
the deleted `oversized` pack was -- one 606 kB file moved to buy the music runtime room to land.
Now the first download is `js/game.js` alone (~0.95 MB of 4.00), and packs arrive in two phases
behind a progress screen. `phase` on each pack below is what the boot code reads, so the
sequence cannot drift from this table:
- `main`: root '', WeChat's first download. Code only. A rule is required to opt INTO it.
- `lobby`: awaited at boot before `new Game(...)`. UI chrome, which is all the login /
menu / mode-select / settings / party / account screens draw.
- `background`: fetched from the lobby, never awaited by anything. `music` only -- 0.84 MB,
and music is the one asset class a game can start without. See MusicPlayer.invalidate():
a deck handed a path inside an unfetched pack plays nothing and never retries, so the
pack's completion clears the director's memo instead of being awaited.
- `run`: fetched from the lobby, AWAITED at the run boundary (entering the forge, the
tutorial, a PvP preview, matchmaking, the arena demo, a replay) behind the same progress
screen. `controllers/ArtGate.ts` owns that gate.
WHY THE UNREACHABLE-TODAY PACKS ARE IN THE `run` PHASE RATHER THAN LAZY AT POINT OF USE.
`biome-ice` / `biome-lightning` / `biome-poison` / `boss` are still justified by content:
theme.ts's BIOME_ID_TO_ELEMENT maps the only authored dungeon ('ember') to 'fire' and
everything without a dungeonConfig (PvP, arena) to 'neutral', so the other three elements
cannot be reached at all today, and 'blightlord' (the only user of skins/boss-core) spawns on
floor 5 only. Awaiting them anyway costs a bounded 654 kB and buys the rule design/12 states:
the set of available textures changes only at a PHASE boundary, never mid-room. Gating each
one at its own point of use would mean re-running preloadBiomeTiles per pack and reasoning
about a half-filled texture map, which is the partial-availability state that rule forbids.
Explicitly NOT deferred beyond the run gate: brute-core and floater-core. `brute` and
`floater` both spawn on FLOOR 1 (world/dungeons/ember/ember_l1_floor_1.json).
`mainPack` and `defaultPack` are two different ideas and used to be one field. `mainPack` is
the package whose root is '' and which WeChat downloads first; `defaultPack` is where a path
no rule matches ends up. Splitting them is what lets the default be `run`, and THAT is the
safety property: a new asset added with no rule can no longer silently enlarge the first
download. It lands in the background instead.
The raw-vs-compressed question stays deliberately open: the only authoritative source is
DevTools' upload dialog, which needs a registered appid and a logged-in session, and pressing
upload PUBLISHES the package. So the gate measures raw bytes, the conservative direction, and
prints the compressed estimate beside it.
A rule matches by path PREFIX against the public-relative path a loader asks for (the
leading-slash form, e.g. '/biome/floor_ice.png'). First matching rule wins; anything
unmatched falls to `defaultPack`.
`limitBytes` on a subpackage is OUR guard, not WeChat's — a standard subpackage has no
individual cap, so this is only here to make a pack that quietly becomes the new dumping
ground fail the gate instead of the 30 MB total.

packs.name: main
packs.note: WeChat's real 4 MB ceiling, and as of 2026-09-01 it holds js/game.js and nothing else. Every byte of art here would be a byte the player downloads before the first frame, so a rule pointing at this pack needs a reason written in the $comment above.

packs.name: lobby
packs.note: ui/* — the one pack a player waits for. Everything the login/menu/mode-select/settings/party/account screens draw, so all of them are fully dressed before `new Game(...)`.

packs.name: music
packs.note: audio/music/*.mp3 — the design/11 loops. 0.84 MB shipped (menu + boss); the third launch track (dungeon.ember) has no master yet, and the limit leaves room for it and not for much else. Never awaited: see MusicPlayer.invalidate().

packs.name: forge
packs.note: weapons/* — mounted-weapon art. In the run phase rather than the lobby one because the forge is the first screen that draws it, and the forge is the gate.

packs.name: run
packs.note: The default pack: rigs, the fire/neutral biome swatches, environment fixtures, SFX — everything a run draws that no other rule claims. A new asset with no rule lands here, which is the safe direction.

packs.name: biome-ice
packs.note: No authored dungeon maps to 'ice' yet (theme.ts BIOME_ID_TO_ELEMENT).

packs.name: biome-lightning
packs.note: No authored dungeon maps to 'lightning' yet.

packs.name: biome-poison
packs.note: No authored dungeon maps to 'poison' yet; design/13 also keeps poison off floor 1 deliberately.
